adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:80 — For user-storage-backed codes the used code is never consumed (no update back to the provider), so allCodesUsed() never becomes true and a single recovery code can be replayed indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds support for storing recovery codes in user storage via `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, which persists the generated codes as a JSON list through `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` (i.e., federated/user-storage path) and skips creating the normal local credential when that succeeds. It also changes consumers (e.g., `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator`) to read federated credentials first via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)`. However, nothing in this diff shows any corresponding write-back/update to federated storage when a code is successfully used. In the only user-storage implementation added/updated here (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid`), validation merely checks membership in the stored JSON list and does not remove/mark a code as used, implying replay is possible for user-storage-backed recovery codes introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:339 — Reference provider isValid accepts any of the generated codes via anyMatch instead of the requested next code and never removes it, modelling a reusable/out-of-order recovery code bypass.

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)`, the newly added Recovery Codes branch deserializes the stored list and returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`. This will accept *any* stored recovery code, regardless of which numbered/next code the UI requests, and it never updates `myUser.recoveryCodes` to remove/mark the used code. That models reusable and out-of-order recovery codes, which is incorrect behavior for one-time recovery codes and can mask issues in the compatibility tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:234 — getCredentials rebuilds the recovery model from the original plaintext list on every call (and drops the stored id), so the next-code number is always #1 and removeStoredCredentialById would get a null id.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/storage/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:241 — Test only performs one login with code #0 and never asserts consumption, rejection on reuse, or that the next login asks for code #1, so it passes while replay is possible.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin`, the flow logs in once and explicitly asserts the requested recovery code index is `0` via `enterRecoveryCodes(..., expectedCode=0, recoveryKeys)` and then signs in. The test never performs a second login, never attempts to reuse the same recovery code, and never asserts that a subsequent login requests the next code (e.g., index `1`) or that replay is rejected. Therefore the finding is correct as a test-coverage gap: the test can pass even if recovery codes are not consumed/invalidated on use.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:125 — When codes are stored in user storage, any pre-existing local DB recovery-codes credential is left in place, leaving stale valid codes alongside the new federated set.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, when `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)` returns true (i.e., user storage/federated update succeeds), the code logs success and does not remove/disable any existing local (Keycloak DB) `recovery-codes` credential. The diff does not show any cleanup step. However, the diff also changes retrieval to prefer federated credentials first (`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(...)` filters `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` and only falls back to local), so the stale local credential is not used on the updated login path. This makes it a real duplication/data-hygiene concern rather than a clearly verifiable functional/security defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/model/RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java:19 — Unchecked Optional.get() on getCredential() still throws NoSuchElementException (500) when neither federated nor local credential exists, e.g. a provider whose getCredentials omits the type.

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`, the diff changes credential lookup to `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` but then immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking presence. If `getCredential(user)` returns `Optional.empty()` (e.g., user has no recovery codes credential in federated or local storage, including cases where a user storage provider does not expose that type), this will throw `NoSuchElementException` and result in a server error (500). This is a concrete, diff-visible crash path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:80 — For federated recovery codes, a successful login never consumes the used code (no update back to user storage), so codes stay reusable and allCodesUsed() never becomes true

adjudication.rationale: The diff only changes RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator to fetch the recovery-codes credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(authenticatedUser), which now checks federated credentials first and falls back to local stored credentials. The diff does not show the code-consumption/update logic for used recovery codes (nor any change to it), so the claim that “successful login never consumes the used code” and that “allCodesUsed() never becomes true” cannot be verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:86 — removeStoredCredentialById is called with the id of a credential that may come from getFederatedCredentialsStream, so it targets local DB storage for a federated credential and cannot delete it

adjudication.rationale: This diff changes RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator to fetch the recovery-codes credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(authenticatedUser), which *prefers* a federated credential from getFederatedCredentialsStream() before falling back to local stored credentials. If the authenticator later calls credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...) using the id from that Optional (as the finding states), then a federated credential id would be passed to a method that targets local DB storage, so it would fail to delete the federated credential. The risky behavior is introduced by the new retrieval order in getCredential().

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — isValid accepts any stored plaintext code rather than the requested next code, and the code is never removed, which breaks one-time and ordered-use semantics

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:113 — createRecoveryCodesCredential takes both credentialModel and generatedCodes, redundant parallel representations of the same data that callers must keep consistent

adjudication.rationale: In the added helper `createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, the method accepts both a `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel credentialModel` and a separate `List<String> generatedCodes`, then stores `generatedCodes` (serialized to JSON) into a `UserCredentialModel` for `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`, but uses `credentialModel` when falling back to `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel)`. This is a diff-grounded API/design concern because callers must ensure `credentialModel` and `generatedCodes` represent the same underlying codes; the helper does not enforce or derive one from the other, making inconsistency possible depending on caller behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the testsuite provider `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` storing recovery codes as plaintext JSON in `CredentialModel.credentialData` (`recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(input.getChallengeResponse())`) and later deserializing and comparing the raw values in `isValid(...)`. This is verifiable from the diff. However, it’s in a testsuite/backwards-compatibility user storage provider (not production credential storage), so it’s more of an insecure example/implementation concern than a product defect introduced by the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — Fixture accepts any code in the list regardless of the requested code number and never consumes used codes, diverging from real one-time-use semantics so the test cannot detect code reuse.

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid() the new RecoveryAuthnCodes branch deserializes a List from credentialData and validates with `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`, which (a) does not check the requested code number and (b) does not remove/consume a successfully used code. This means the test user-storage fixture will accept reuse of the same recovery code and can’t catch regressions around one-time-use semantics, even though the UI flow presents a specific code index.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:237 — getCredentials rebuilds the model via createFromValues on every call (fresh/unstable id, no used-state), so the authenticator's allCodesUsed/removeStoredCredentialById path for federated credentials is never exercised realistically.

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage#getCredentials, the returned RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel is reconstructed each time via createFromValues(JsonSerialization.readValue(...), createdDate, userLabel) and does not propagate the originally stored CredentialModel id (set in updateCredential via KeycloakModelUtils.generateId() on myUser.recoveryCodes). From the diff we can verify the id is ignored, so any flow relying on a stable federated credential id (e.g., deletion by id) would not be realistically represented by this test provider. The finding’s broader claim about specific authenticator paths (allCodesUsed/removeStoredCredentialById) is plausible but not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/storage/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:241 — Only the happy path (one login with code 0) is tested; no coverage for invalid code rejection, reuse of an already-used code, second login requesting the next code, or exhausting all codes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new recovery-codes behavior (e.g., CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential storing JSON codes in user storage vs local, and RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential checking federated then local). The new test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin()` only exercises a single successful login using the first requested code (`enterRecoveryCodes(... expectedCode=0 ...)`) and does not cover important edge/flow behaviors implied by this feature (invalid code rejection, reuse prevention, subsequent login requesting next code index, or exhaustion). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap for newly introduced nontrivial logic, not a verifiable runtime defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:126 — New createRecoveryCodesCredential fallback branch (user storage returns false -> local DB) and the RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential federated-first lookup have no tests confirming local-user behavior is unchanged.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new branching behavior for recovery codes: `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` first calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` and only if that returns false falls back to `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)`. Also `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` now prefers federated credentials before local stored credentials. The only added test (`testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin`) asserts recovery codes are created in *user storage* (federated) via `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageFactory.hasRecoveryCodes`, but there is no test in this diff that exercises/validates the fallback-to-local-DB branch or confirms local (non-federated) user behavior remains correct under the new lookup/creation logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/model/RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java:19 — Unchecked Optional.get() remains with no test covering a user lacking any recovery credential (federated or stored).

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`, the diff replaces a direct stored-credential lookup with `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` but still immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without any presence check. `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` can return `Optional.empty()` if the user has neither federated nor locally stored recovery-codes credentials, which would throw `NoSuchElementException` at runtime. The added tests cover setup/login when credentials exist, but nothing in the diff ensures this bean is only constructed when the Optional is present.
